finding: Creativity that produces results is not a trait to prompt for; it is four mechanical moves against four measured failure modes. (1) Einstellung: name the obvious answer and forbid it, because it blocks the better one while the solver believes they are still searching. (2) Marginality: solve it as a distant field would, because field distance positively predicts winning solutions. (3) Production blocking: generate alone before combining, because interacting groups produce less than the same people separately. (4) Mode collapse: ask for a distribution of options with probabilities, not one answer. The bound on all four: novelty at ideation does NOT survive execution -- the ranking flipped after 43 experts spent 100+ hours -- so an option's value is novelty times the probability it survives execution, never novelty alone.
angles: seven searches; four peer-reviewed publishers (PLOS ONE, INFORMS, Basic and Applied Social Psychology, Psychological Bulletin) on the psychology, three arXiv primaries on the machine side; the ideation and execution findings come from two SEPARATE studies that disagree, which is what makes the discount measured rather than assumed
gaps: No study found that measures whether these four moves work on an LLM agent specifically. Einstellung, marginality, production blocking and incubation were all measured on humans; Verbalized Sampling and the two arXiv papers are on models but test none of the four. The transfer is an assumption, and inventor.md is the experiment rather than the conclusion.
No measurement of what the forbid-the-obvious move COSTS: it may discard a correct cheap answer. No source found that prices that.
